explainer_reply:
Looking at these examples, I notice a strong recurring pattern:

- Many activations are on numbers that form **years** (1906, 1856, 1834, 2004, 2013, 2019)
- Many are on **full dates** (May 16, 2017; February 2, 2015; December 13, 2004)
- Several are on **timestamps** (19:27:00, 14:29, 02:53:02, 20:43)
- The punctuation activated (commas, dashes, colons, parentheses) is typically the **formatting within dates/timestamps**: "1998-01-11", "Wednesday, March 4, 2009", "(2019)", "Sent: Friday, August 11, 2006"
- Month names (May, June, Nov, Apr) and day names (Tuesday, Friday) also activate when part of date expressions
- Contexts include citations, forum signatures, blog post headers, and database timestamps

[EXPLANATION]: Tokens that are components of date and timestamp expressions, including years, month and day names, day numbers, and the punctuation (commas, dashes, colons, parentheses) used to format dates in citations, signatures, headers, and timestamps.
